analysis:
Two files were reviewed. No finding qualifies on the visible evidence, but coverage is incomplete.

docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md: base text was supplied only for lines 280-422 and head text for the whole file. Head lines 280-422 look identical to base, so the edit is in head lines 1-279, which cannot be compared against base. The head text still describes the unchanged T-041 posture: HMAC lookup tags (line 62-63), a 1800 s TTL cap (line 276), the dev-versus-prod KEK service and namespace split (lines 20 and 61), and a root-wide write ledger (lines 34-37, 288-298). It makes no claim that loosens T-041 or SEC-035, and TTL/limit constants and the SEC-035 sign-off requirement are unchanged.

provider-swift/Package.swift (patch): adds a new ProviderBuildEnvironment target that carries the DARKBLOOM_ENV_DEV define. ProviderAppAttest, ProviderCoreFoundation and ProviderCore now depend on it, and ProviderCore no longer receives the define directly (its swiftSettings were removed). The patch comment says ProviderCore re-exports the module. Residual risk for the next pass: a file in ProviderCore, or in any target not given the define, that still uses '#if DARKBLOOM_ENV_DEV' now compiles as prod. A dev build could then silently use the prod KEK Keychain service (io.darkbloom.kv.kek.v1), the prod cache namespace 'darkbloom', or the prod coordinator, which would break the dev/prod isolation the doc describes. The Sources/ProviderBuildEnvironment sources, the BuildEnvironment implementation and the call sites were not supplied. Only ProviderCoreFoundationTests got the new dependency, so other test targets may not exercise the dev define.

Coverage limit: the new target's sources, the unchanged callers and the base text for doc lines 1-279 were not provided. Callers still using '#if DARKBLOOM_ENV_DEV' should be grepped outside the ProviderBuildEnvironment module.
